summary: A steel-and-terra-cotta tower on a concrete pier in northern Lake Michigan, lit in 1910 to replace a steam lightship that ice forced off station each winter.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Record's first_lit 1891 is the date lightship No. 56 went on station (22 Oct per the Board's list, 24 Oct per Lighthouse Friends and Pepper); the tower was lit 1 Sept 1910.
The record's duplicate 'built 1910' and two first_lit/nrhp_listed entries (1984 and 1999) are not explained by sources read; NRHP nomination PDF is not digitised.

notes_for_editor: Source disagreements stated in the story: lightship date (22 vs 24 Oct 1891); range (20 nm per 1912 report vs 28 per Pepper); submarine bell end (1914 Pepper, 1916 LHF; Commissioner 1917 lists it among signals discontinued in fiscal 1917); spiral paint (1954 LHF vs 1990 Pepper); lens removal (1983 vs 1987); first keeper (USLHS lists J. M. Marshall in 1910 before Olsen; LHF says Olsen was first); distance from Waugoshance (4.5 mi from the lighthouse per LHF, 2.6 mi from the island per Pepper). The 1912 Commissioner description was read through Lighthouse Friends, which reproduces it, not in the original; the story cites it that way. Lighthouse Friends gives the auction as 15 July to 25 September 'in 2015' in one sentence (a typo); the owners say September 2016. The NRHP nomination (84001391) is not digitised, so listing dates (record shows 1984 and 1999) are unverified. The record's other_names include '1910' and 'Current', which look like scraping debris. The Ida L entry: Lighthouse Friends names the launch; the Commissioner's 1915 life-saving table is garbled in OCR and the vessel was not matched by column position. The 1912 and 1915 Bulletin pennant list was not matched by position; only the index entry is used. Index to Bulletin 1924-29 lists B. D. Preston as keeper at White Shoal (not in the USLHS roster) and a rescue/assist by him; not used. USCG names (1960-70) are from the USLHS roster only. The 1915 Commissioner table's page numbers (printed p. 64, scan 69) and 1917 report p.52 were taken from corpus grep labels.
